pill.desc: clear, colorless to slightly yellowish solution in a single-dose pen

clues.kinetics: Subcutaneous bioavailability ranges from 55% to 77%. It is expected to be broken down into small peptides and amino acids by ordinary catabolic pathways.
clues.substance: A sterile, preservative-free solution for subcutaneous use. Its molecular mass is about 151 kDa, and both heavy chains carry oligosaccharide chains.
clues.product: Approved under a BLA as 300 mg/2 mL and 150 mg/mL pens and syringes, plus a 75 mg/0.5 mL syringe; maintenance dosing is every 4 weeks.
clues.safety: No boxed warning. Contraindicated after a serious hypersensitivity reaction to it, and nasopharyngitis and upper respiratory tract infection were reported by over 1% of adults in its trials.
clues.indication: Moderate to severe plaque psoriasis, active psoriatic arthritis, ankylosing spondylitis, non-radiographic axial spondyloarthritis, enthesitis-related arthritis and hidradenitis suppurativa.
clues.mechanism: It selectively binds the cytokine interleukin-17A and inhibits its interaction with the IL-17 receptor. This reduces the release of proinflammatory cytokines and chemokines.

tell: A human IgG1 antibody to IL-17A with a half-life of 22 to 31 days, supplied as a 300 mg single-dose pen.
